title: Equal aids: true of prevenient grace, not of cooperating grace
source_text: XC. Porro quum Doctor iste dicit, si duobus hominibus aequalia auxilia ex parte Dei dentur, fieri posse ut unus pro sua libertate convertatur, & alter non: monet id se intelligere de auxiliis gratiae praevenientis, qua praeveniens est. Nam si agatur de gratiae ejusdem auxiliis, quatenus est cooperans, id est, quatenus per eam Deus influit in actum quem homo libere elicit, non amplius verum est, aequali auxilio dato, unum converti, alterum non converti. Siquidem impossibile est aliquem non converti, & tamen Deum in eo efficere, cum libero ejus arbitrio, conversionis actum. Sed quoniam gratia praeveniens & cooperans reapse sunt unum & idem, & gratiae cooperatio a liberi nostri arbitrii cooperatione pendet, non secus ac concursus & influxus cujusvis habitus, ab operatione potentiae cui inest: simpliciter & absolute loquendo dicendum putat, unum cum aequalibus, aut etiam cum minoribus auxiliis pro sua libertate converti, ac salvari, quando alius neque convertitur neque salvatur. Licet si in summo rigore loquamur, dici non debeat cum aequalibus gratiae auxiliis unum converti, alterum non converti: quoniam in eo qui convertitur est influxus quidam gratiae, qui in alio non est; ille nimirum qui pendet a liberi nostri arbitrii consensu.
pass_a_gloss: XC. Moreover when that Doctor says, if equal aids be given to two men on the part of God, it can come about that one by his liberty is converted, & the other not: he warns that he understands this of the aids of prevenient grace, as it is prevenient. For if it be a question of the aids of the same grace, as far as it is cooperating, that is, as far as through it God flows into the act which man freely elicits, it is no longer true, equal aid being given, that one is converted, the other not converted. Since it is impossible that someone be not converted, & yet that God effect in him, with his free choice, the act of conversion. But since prevenient & cooperating grace are really one & the same, & the cooperation of grace depends on the cooperation of our free choice, not otherwise than the concurrence & influx of any habit, on the operation of the power in which it is: simply & absolutely speaking he thinks it must be said, that one with equal, or even with lesser aids by his liberty is converted, and saved, when another is neither converted nor saved. Although if we speak in the highest rigour, it ought not to be said that with equal aids of grace one is converted, the other not converted: since in him who is converted there is a certain influx of grace, which in the other is not; namely that which depends on the consent of our free choice.
pass_b_english: Thesis XC. When Molina says that if God gives two people equal aids, one may be converted by his own freedom and the other not, he warns that he means the aids of prevenient grace, taken as prevenient. If we speak of that same grace as cooperating, that is, as the grace through which God flows into the act a person freely elicits, it is no longer true that with equal aid one is converted and the other is not. It is impossible for someone not to be converted while God is nevertheless producing in him, together with his free choice, the act of conversion.

Yet prevenient and cooperating grace are in reality one and the same, and the cooperation of grace depends on the cooperation of our free choice, just as the concurrence and influence of any habit depends on the working of the power it resides in. So, speaking simply and absolutely, he thinks one must say that a person is converted and saved by his freedom with equal or even smaller aids, while another is neither converted nor saved. Speaking with the utmost strictness, though, one should not say that with equal aids of grace one is converted and the other not, since in the one converted there is an influence of grace not present in the other: the influence that depends on the consent of our free choice.

lemmas.latin: cum aequalibus, aut etiam cum minoribus auxiliis
lemmas.gloss: with equal, or even with lesser aids

choices.why: Molina's distinction of one grace under two respects: as it goes before consent (prevenient) and as it flows into the act with consent (cooperating).
